name: Sulaymān al-Tājir's Persian Gulf to China voyage account
summary: An Arab merchant identified as Sulaymān al-Tājir ('the Merchant') writes the earliest surviving Arabic eyewitness account of voyaging from Siraf and Basra to Khānfū (Guangzhou). The Akhbār al-Ṣīn wa-l-Hind ('Reports of China and India'), expanded by Abu Zayd al-Sirafi around 916, is the foundational text of the medieval Arabic-language geography of the Indian Ocean and the Tang treaty-port system.

_quarry.structural_significance: Earliest Arabic eyewitness on the Indian Ocean / South China Sea trade route; documents the substantial Persian and Arab merchant presence at Khanfu before the Huang Chao massacre (879) drove the Sino-Arab maritime trade temporarily to Kalah on the Malay Peninsula.
